title: Francis Bacon, New Atlantis (1627)

source.publisher: Project Gutenberg (ebook #2434, Michael Pullen and William Fishburne)
source.license: Public domain (Francis Bacon died 1626; Project Gutenberg text)

summary: Bacon's unfinished utopia of an island, Bensalem, ruled by a scientific foundation. It uses the name Atlantis, and calls America "the great Atlantis", but is not a theory about Plato's island. A key source for how the name travelled.

tool.name: hand-built (PageIndex format)
tool.method: Hand-built tree from the paragraph sequence of the text: the book has no chapter headings, so sections follow the story. No language model was used.

tree.title: Introductory note
tree.summary: Rawley's and the editor's note on the work, published in 1627 after Bacon's death and left unfinished.

tree.title: The voyage and arrival at Bensalem
tree.summary: A ship from Peru bound for China and Japan is blown off course, finds an unknown island, and is allowed to land after the crew answers questions and promises.

tree.title: The Strangers' House, the ark and the letter of St Bartholomew
tree.summary: The crew is housed and cared for. A Christian ark arrives long ago with books and a letter from St Bartholomew, which explains the island's conversion.

tree.title: The Governor's account: ancient navigation and the great Atlantis
tree.summary: The Governor says the island traded with the world 3,000 years ago and that the great Atlantis (America) flourished, then was destroyed by flood, leaving a thin and rude population.

tree.title: King Solamona and the founding of Salomon's House
tree.summary: About 1,900 years ago King Solamona closed the island to foreign travel except for fact-finding voyages and founded Salomon's House, a society devoted to natural knowledge.

tree.title: Life in Bensalem: the Feast of the Family and the laws of marriage
tree.summary: The narrator sees the Feast of the Family, an honour to fathers of thirty descendants, and talks to the Jewish merchant Joabin about Bensalem's chastity and marriage customs.

tree.title: The Father of Salomon's House
tree.summary: A Father of Salomon's House arrives in procession, and the narrator is chosen to meet him privately.

tree.title: Salomon's House: the end of the foundation, caves, towers, houses and instruments
tree.summary: The Father describes the aim of the foundation, then its caves, towers, lakes, engines, houses of health, orchards, gardens, workshops, light and sound, and other places of experiment.

tree.title: Salomon's House: its staff, merchants of light, and ordinances
tree.summary: The Father lists the fellows and their duties, the "merchants of light" who travel abroad, and the rites and galleries, then blesses the narrator. The text breaks off.
